name: Banjara Hills
tagline: Rocky ridges, embassies and the city's smartest cafes
description: Banjara Hills climbs a granite ridge west of the centre, its numbered Road No. 1 to 14 lined with consulates, designer boutiques, hospitals and villas behind high walls. Road No. 12 and the Jubilee Hills border hold most of the specialty coffee shops and coworking spaces. It is central, green and expensive by Hyderabad standards.
bestFor: Nomads who want the best cafes and restaurants without commuting out to the tech corridor.
pros: Roughly equidistant from Old City and HITEC City
Top private hospitals and clinics nearby
cons: Rents are among the highest in Hyderabad
Road No. 1 traffic is heavy most of the day
Steep hilly streets make walking a chore

name: Jubilee Hills
tagline: Film-industry villas and quiet leafy lanes
description: Jubilee Hills sits just north-west of Banjara Hills, a planned residential colony of large villas, film-industry homes and gated apartment blocks arranged around numbered roads and Jubilee Hills Check Post. Streets are wide, tree-lined and calm, with fine-dining restaurants, clubs and KBR National Park's five-kilometre walking loop on the edge.
bestFor: Longer stays that prioritise a quiet apartment, greenery and a short hop to the tech corridor.
pros: Calm residential streets with mature trees
KBR Park for daily walks and running
Fifteen to twenty minutes to HITEC City off-peak
cons: Expensive and short on budget food options
Sparse public transport, you rely on cabs
Little street life, feels sleepy at night

name: HITEC City & Madhapur
tagline: Glass towers, coworking and the fastest internet
description: HITEC City and neighbouring Madhapur form Hyderabad's tech corridor: Cyber Towers, Mindspace and the campuses of Microsoft, Amazon and Google, ringed by serviced apartments, malls and a heavy concentration of coworking spaces. Internet is the most reliable in the city and the Blue Line metro runs to Ameerpet and the centre.
bestFor: Remote workers who want reliable fibre, coworking desks and other professionals to meet.
pros: Best broadband and most coworking options
Serviced apartments built for short leases
Metro connection into the city centre
cons: Severe rush-hour gridlock on the main roads
Corporate and characterless outside the malls
Long, expensive trip to the Old City

name: Begumpet
description: Begumpet runs along the old airport road between Hussain Sagar lake and Ameerpet, a mix of mid-century apartment blocks, business hotels, the Secunderabad Club and rows of small restaurants. It has its own metro and suburban rail stations, which makes it one of the few Hyderabad addresses where you can get by without a car.
bestFor: Budget-conscious nomads who want metro access and mid-range rents near the middle of the city.
pros: Metro and suburban rail on the doorstep
Rents well below Banjara and Jubilee Hills
Central position, good access in all directions
cons: Noisy, congested main roads and flyovers
Air quality is poor along the corridor

name: Old City & Charminar
tagline: Qutb Shahi heritage, bazaars and the cheapest rooms
description: The Old City fans out from the Charminar into Laad Bazaar's bangle shops, the Mecca Masjid and lanes of biryani houses and Irani cafes. It is the most historic and most densely packed part of Hyderabad, overwhelmingly local, and rooms cost a fraction of what the western suburbs charge.
bestFor: Travellers on a tight budget who want heritage and street food over comfort and connectivity.
pros: Cheapest accommodation and food in the city
Monuments and bazaars on your doorstep
Metro Green Line reaches the northern edge
cons: Very congested, noisy and hard to walk
Slower internet and few work-friendly cafes
